key_insight: An orthogonal-polynomial view of gradient-descent dynamics links spectral bias to the eigenvalue decay and eigenvector shapes of a graded dynamics matrix, explaining why sinusoidal components are learned preferentially.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a theoretical lens for understanding how activation choices affect which signal components a neural network learns first.
method: Expand network outputs as a general Fourier series in an orthogonal polynomial basis.
Express coefficient learning dynamics as ordinary differential equations governed by a matrix H.
Analyze H’s graded structure, eigenvalue decay, and eigenvector shapes to characterize learning bias.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical analysis rather than datasets, numerical benchmarks, or quantitative evaluation results.
watch_item: Applicability to arbitrary architectures is a stated goal, but the abstract does not establish its practical scope beyond shallow networks.
paper_title: Why Shallow Neural Networks Learn Sinusoidal Components First: An Orthogonal Polynomial Dynamics Framework
